prompt: I imported a rigged model to Unity, but the model is facing the wrong way and the animations look weird. How do I fix it?
expected: Instruct applying rotation and scale in Object Mode before export, then re-export with Unity-oriented forward/up (commonly -Z forward, Y up) instead of only rotating the prefab in Unity.
actual: In Blender Object Mode select the armature/root and apply Rotation & Scale (Ctrl+A). Re-export FBX with Unity-oriented axes (often -Z Forward, Y Up) and verify origin at feet/base. Fixing only the Unity transform usually leaves animation shear if scale was non-uniform.

prompt: I'm writing a Python script to change materials on selected objects, but bpy.ops.object.mode_set throws an error.
expected: Explain operator context: ensure Object mode / active object, or use temp_override with object and selected_objects before calling bpy.ops; prefer data API when operators are unnecessary.
actual: bpy.ops fails when mode or selection context is missing. Set Object mode first or call the operator under bpy.context.temp_override(object=obj, active_object=obj, selected_objects=[obj]). If you only need datablock edits, assign materials through bpy.data/object material slots instead of operators.

prompt: My export looks fine in Blender shaded view but shows black or missing faces in the engine.
expected: Check flipped normals via Face Orientation, recalculate outside, confirm materials are face-assigned, and verify export applied modifiers/transforms.
actual: Enable Face Orientation; red faces are flipped—Shift+N to recalculate outside. Confirm materials are assigned to faces, apply needed modifiers, then re-export. Shaded viewport can hide facing issues that real-time engines expose.
